track_S.mechanism: semantic recompilation — freeze behaviour, build canonical cores, facade, migrate, delete internals and facades
blocking_contracts: Model-family unification forbidden until a shared LayerOp IR proves bit-exact argmax/top-k and <=2% decode p50 on both families
~27,500 LOC of live pack/parity/gravity science is not repeated architecture
Dual event models are must_not_delete until the Bridge lane

track_V.mechanism: minimal vertical slices — build the smallest complete path, measure what the current tree carries that a slice would never need
track_V.blocking_contract: Model families are distinct executors at jaccard < 0.11, plus ~129k of laboratory sealed science and the HIDE product floor. The expansion to cover the full capability matrix consumes the residue.

convergence.shared_first_blocking_contract: Model families require separate executors until a LayerOp IR proves bit-exactness and performance parity. Both tracks name it independently.
convergence.significance: Two architectures designed from opposite directions -- one shrinking existing subsystems, one building minimal paths from capability -- land 11,200 apart. That agreement is evidence about the shape of the problem, not about either designer.

selection.why: Its projection is lower (394,000 against 405,200), it clears the 400k rung where Track S does not, and its two measured slices are the sharpest concrete leads in either design: the campaign path measures 2,800 minimal against 95,766 current, and the adapter/Bridge path 3,500 against 21,430.
selection.caveat: V's own verdict is slices_rebuild_most_of_it. Its 310,000-line expansion is what makes the projection realistic rather than aspirational, and it is the number a prototype must test.

next: Prototype the campaign slice, which is the highest-leverage MEASURED claim in either track: 2,800 lines against 95,766. If a slice that small carries the capability, the laboratory collapses. If it cannot, the reason is the first precise behaviour contract this arc is required to find.
